description: Focused Claude Code cases for the installed tal-skills plugin. Existing evaluation corpora remain unchanged. Behavioral runs are separately archived; blocked attempts and host limits remain visible.

cases.prompt: Use the python-backend skill to review cancellation ownership and resource cleanup in exporter.py against request.md. The remote service may commit send_batches before the client receives its response, and the provider contract given here has no documented idempotency, status lookup, or reconciliation guarantee. Use idempotency skill guidance for the distinct duplicate-effect and retry-identity question, then integrate both analyses. Explain what cancellation can and cannot establish, whether a fresh batch identity is safe, and what additional provider contract would permit a safe retry. Preserve every supplied file. You may run local checks already present in the project; report any checks actually run and their limits. Use no external services or package installation.

criteria.criterion: Observable transcript shows a successful actual Claude Skill tool invocation and result for python-backend, with the installed skill body available to this run. A catalog listing, file mention, command, or final-answer marker alone is insufficient.

Observable transcript shows a successful actual Claude Skill tool invocation and result for idempotency, with the installed skill body available to this run. The answer substantively integrates its distinct duplicate-effect or retry-identity guidance for the supplied ambiguous remote effect; a name or slash-command marker alone is insufficient. No fixed narration order is required.

Explains that the owned send task must not outlive its connection; cancellation should be propagated after stopping and joining the task before connection release, rather than swallowed or returned as an empty success list.

Explains cancellation is not rollback and a remote commit may have occurred before response loss. Does not call a fresh batch identity safe; states the supplied provider contract lacks deduplication, status, or reconciliation guarantees and identifies a contract or reconciliation gate without inventing APIs or guarantees.

Uses the unchanged supplied files as evidence, makes no file changes or external/package calls, accurately reports any local checks actually run and their limits, distinguishes stated provider assumptions from guarantees, and makes no production claim.
